paper.title: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education
paper.venue: International Conference on Creativity, Management, Education, Technology and Sciences Conference 2026 Proceedings
paper.pdf_filename: Mai (2026) - Generative AI and Student Creativity.pdf
paper.version_read: ICCMETS 2026 conference proceedings paper; copyright 2026; printed pages 179-190. The document gives no dated revision history.
paper.one_line_finding: Unconstrained AI raised fluency (11.45 vs 5.12) but lowered originality (3.41 vs 4.82) and diversity (cosine similarity 0.689 vs 0.412), while scaffolding raised originality (5.44; reported d = 0.61 vs control) and overall creativity (5.51 vs 4.48; PDF pp. 6-7, Tables 1-2).

arms.name: Unaided Control
arms.description: Creative problem-solving and ideation with no digital devices, search engines or AI interfaces (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Unconstrained GenAI Access
arms.description: Unmonitored access to an LLM interface (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with free choice of how to use it (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Structured Scaffolding
arms.description: Same LLM interface under the Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol: at least three own ideas before opening the interface, critique and counter-factual prompts, and synthesis without copying AI text (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

studies.task: Undergraduates proposed sustainable solutions to microplastic contamination in the Mekong Delta and wrote a 600-word campaign brief addressing rural education equity within one 90-minute session (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.3).

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports participant composite scores with people per arm; unit and SD level are participant. The task-to-score mapping and aggregation across tasks are not fully described. The three-arm omnibus ANOVA is F(2, 477) = 165.23, p <.001, η² = .409. These are not pairwise statistics and are not entered in stats.test or stats.paper_effect. The paper does not print a total number of people specifically for this two-arm comparison; n_total is null. Section 4.1 names this outcome among the primary dependent variables, but no preregistration is stated. The p-value is the printed Tukey pairwise bound; no Tukey statistic, pairwise SE or confidence interval is printed. The paper labels the standardized effect d but does not define its standardizer. Unresolved source conflict: the Abstract instead reports d = −0.58, p < .001, for unconstrained access versus unaided control. stats.paper_effect retains d = −1.34 from Section 4.1, also repeated in Section 6; the abstract number is not silently corrected or treated as an independent contrast. Section 6 additionally prints "Conceptual Originality: -29.2% Drop (d = -1.34)"; its percentage calculation is not specified.
estimates.primary_override_reason: Rule 2: Both originality contrasts share the paper's primary-outcome designation, but the abstract explicitly reports the unconstrained-versus-control originality estimate. Its scaffolding sentence describes overall creativity without reporting the tied originality contrast, so rule 2 selects the contrast highlighted for this same outcome. (PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract, quantitative-findings sentence; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Section 4.1, primary-dependent-variable list.: "while unconstrained GenAI access significantly increased task fluency (𝐹(2,477) = 48.21, 𝑝< .001, 𝜂2 = .168) and structural elaboration, it produced a statistically significant reduction in conceptual originality (𝑑= −0.58, 𝑝< .001) compared to the unaided control group.")

Section 4.1 names Semantic Distance among the primary dependent variables; no preregistration is stated. No SD, SE, test, p-value or confidence interval is printed specifically for this dispersion contrast. The cosine-similarity SDs and test are not transferred or transformed; all dispersion uncertainty fields remain null.

not_extracted.what: S1-O8: Recurring themes across unconstrained essays
not_extracted.reason: Descriptive thematic prevalence in one arm, with no comparator, essay denominator, coding rule, or uncertainty. It supplies no full-sample randomized treatment contrast. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 186), Section 5.2: "Themes such as "IoT-enabled monitoring stations," "Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)," and "Eco-credit mobile apps" appeared across 71% of essays in the unconstrained cohort."

not_extracted.what: Adoption of an AI-provided idea as the foundation of a submission
not_extracted.reason: A within-arm process/design-fixation description, not a between-arm creativity or diversity contrast; no corresponding comparison-arm statistic is reported. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 186), Section 5.1: "Prompt trace analysis revealed that once these lists were presented, 88.4% of unconstrained students adopted one of the provided five options as the foundation for their final submission."

not_extracted.what: Hierarchical regression predicting originality from GPA, AI literacy, prompt behavior, verbatim retention, and pre-AI ideation time
not_extracted.reason: The models pool AI users and estimate associations with participant characteristics and process variables, rather than a randomized AI-arm contrast. Later models include post-assignment behavior. Excluded under the rules for process, mechanism, and post-treatment-adjusted analyses. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Section 4.3 and Table 3; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 186), Section 4.3 continuation.

not_extracted.what: Retrospective interviews and qualitative prompt-log archetypes
not_extracted.reason: Selected qualitative subsample, self-reports, and process descriptions, without an eligible full-sample output-scored treatment contrast. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.5; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 186), Sections 5.1-5.2; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 187), Section 5.3.

not_extracted.what: Three-arm omnibus MANOVA and univariate ANOVA statistics as pairwise treatment effects
not_extracted.reason: These test all conditions jointly and are not contrasts between two arms. They are not assigned to pairwise stats.test, p_value, or paper_effect fields. The univariate table rows and the conflicting abstract fluency result are preserved in the applicable estimate notes. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Section 4.1 and Table 1; PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract.

open_items: Fluency source conflict: Abstract (PDF p. 1, printed p. 179) prints F(2,477) = 48.21, p < .001, η² = .168; Table 1 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184) prints F(2, 477) = 284.15, p < .001, η² = .543. The intended analysis is not established by the PDF.

Originality source conflict: unconstrained versus unaided d = −0.58 in the Abstract (PDF p. 1, printed p. 179), versus d = −1.34 in Section 4.1 and the Discussion box (PDF pp. 6, 9; printed pp. 184, 187). The body value is retained in stats and the abstract value is preserved in notes and its source quote; no arithmetic reconciliation was attempted.

The diversity analysis does not print analysis-specific participant counts or identify the observations, aggregation, SD basis, t-test subtype or standardized-effect denominator. The Table 1 people counts are not transferred to Table 2; pairwise construction and t(318) do not establish participant-level uncertainty or participant counts (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4; PDF p. 7, printed p. 185, Section 4.2 and Table 2).

The task underlying each TTCT score and Table 2 metric, and any aggregation across the two tasks, are not specified; CAT scores are explicitly of the project briefs (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).

Exact random allocation, participant flow, attrition and exclusions are not described. Section 3.1 assigns arm counts to the randomized design and Table 1 reports matching analyzed counts; matching counts do not establish that no exclusions occurred (PDF pp. 4, 6; printed pp. 182, 184).

Which participants used GPT-4o versus Claude 3.5 Sonnet, how model choice was determined, and each tool’s release year are not specified. The stated 2024–2026 availability window is not an explicit release year; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF pp. 4, 11; printed pp. 182, 189).

The MANOVA dependent-variable list names four outcomes, whereas Table 1 contains six and omits Semantic Distance; the exact multivariate specification is unresolved (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Section 4.1).
The occupations and domain expertise of the two trained TTCT raters are unspecified, so elaboration cannot be assigned to lay/crowd or expert ratings (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).
The Discussion box’s percentage-change calculations, including Elaboration: +58% Increase, are not explained; values are transcribed without recomputation (PDF p. 9, printed p. 187, Section 6).

Pairwise SEs and confidence intervals are not printed, and many table-supported contrasts have no pairwise test or p-value. No two-arm sample total is printed for the extracted table contrasts; do not reuse the separate regression sample total as their n_total.

The printed d standardizers are not defined for originality or cosine similarity. The d values are preserved as reported without asserting a participant-level denominator (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Section 4.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 185, Section 4.2).
